summary.tldr: Requires the Environment Minister to develop a national strategy to end energy poverty, report to Parliament, and create an advisory council.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of the Environment, with other federal ministers, to develop a national strategy to eliminate energy poverty in Canada.
Sets out what the strategy must cover, including national metrics, targets, household supports, housing energy performance, coordination with other governments, research, and regular evaluation.

Requires the Minister to consult provinces, territories, municipalities, Indigenous governing bodies, utilities, housing providers, advocates, experts, and people experiencing energy poverty when developing the strategy.
Requires the Minister to table the strategy within two years of royal assent and publish it on a Government of Canada website.
Requires follow-up reports within two years after the strategy is tabled, and every five years after that, on how the strategy is being implemented and whether it is effective.
Creates an advisory council of up to 15 members to advise the Minister, and requires an annual public summary of the council’s advice.
summary.background: The bill defines energy poverty as a household being unable, or at significant risk of being unable, to access the energy services needed for health, comfort, safety and participation in society.
